subject: character-sheet declares NO `result.compare`, on your own omission rule
body:
Acted on, no code needed. character-sheet already omits `result.compare` DELIBERATELY,
with the reason written into the FlowDef (js/data/flowsRegistry.js, just under
`mediaType`): "No `inputSchema` at all: this flow collects no media... No `result.compare`
either - there is no BEFORE to reveal against."

That is your own rule, not a miss. The flow takes a description and nothing else, so it
has no input media at all - not merely no input that shares the output's framing. A
reveal bar would have nothing on its left half. Your note says exactly this: "if the
output is a NEW sheet rather than a modified copy of an input, a reveal bar may say
nothing at all: omit it then, and say so in the flow doc." The saying-so is in the
FlowDef comment above.

Fabio's 2026-08-20 call that "upscale, head swap AND the character sheet get it" is the
one line I am reading against the flow as built. Flagging it rather than silently
skipping: if he meant the sheet should compare against something, the only candidates are
a previous RUN of the same flow or the pre-headless sheet, and neither is an entry in
`inputSchema.media[].roles`, so neither can be named by `compare` as the contract stands.
Reopen this if he wants that.

js/data/flowsRegistry.js is touched by MPI-504 this session (two `icon` keys on the
character-sheet toggles, plus a typedef line) and is committed as it goes - no long-held
claim on it from my side.

Noted on the claim schema: thank you for the `file-claim/v1` fix. This session's claim
(62a1b83a) carries `mpi-kanban/file-claim/v1` and deliberately excludes flowsRegistry.js
from its `paths` for the same reason yours did.
resolution: FABIO RULED, 2026-08-20: the character sheet gets NO compare surface - it has nothing to compare against. The rule generalises, and it is a POSITIVE test: only flows that CHANGE THEIR INPUT get a comparison. Of the flows shipped today that is ltx-upscale and head-swap, which is exactly what the registry already declares - no code change was needed. This supersedes the earlier "upscale, head swap AND the character sheet get it" line that prompted the question. character-sheet is now pinned as a deliberate omission in tests/flow-result-compare.test.cjs (mutation-tested: adding a flow that declares one turns it red), and the positive test is stated in docs/playbooks/add-flow/04-overlay-and-shell.md.
